title: Graphs: networks, traversals, and shortest paths

chapters.title: Breadth-first search: exploring layer by layer
facts: Breadth-first search (BFS) uses a queue to explore neighbours level by level in O(V + E) time
graph G = (V, E) consists of a set of vertices V and a set of edges E

chapters.title: Depth-first search: following paths to the end
facts: Depth-first search (DFS) uses recursion or a stack to explore as deep as possible along each branch in O(V + E) time

chapters.title: Shortest path on unweighted graphs
facts: BFS finds the shortest path in terms of edge count in an unweighted graph

chapters.title: Representing graphs: adjacency list vs matrix
facts: adjacency list stores an array of linked lists or dynamic arrays, using O(V + E) memory
checking if an edge exists takes O(1) time
